sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Microsoft Azure interview questions cover the platform common in enterprise Java backend roles — Azure Spring Apps for managed Spring Boot, AKS and Azure Container Registry, Azure Functions for serverless Java, the storage stack (Blob, SQL Database, Cosmos DB), the messaging stack (Service Bus vs Event Hubs), Key Vault and Managed Identity for passwordless auth, Azure Active Directory with Spring Security, and Application Insights for observability. Use this page when the job description mentions Azure or Microsoft-shop tooling.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Azure = **enterprise-first** Microsoft cloud.

- **Compute** — Azure Spring Apps (managed Spring Boot), AKS, Functions.
- **Data** — Azure SQL, Cosmos DB (multi-model), Blob Storage.
- **Messaging** — Service Bus (queues / topics), Event Hubs (streams).
- **Identity** — Entra ID (formerly AAD); managed identities for services.
- **Observability** — Application Insights tied to Azure Monitor.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:

- **Azure api and observability** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Cosmos DB partition key** — hot partitions blow your RU bill; choose carefully.
- **Managed Identity** > connection strings.
- **Key Vault** + reference syntax in App Settings — pulls secrets at runtime.
- **Spring on Azure** — Azure Spring Apps gives you Eureka + Config without standing them up.
- **Hybrid scenarios** — Azure Arc / ExpressRoute show up in enterprise interviews.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd deploy Spring Boot to Azure Spring Apps or AKS, store transactional data in Azure SQL, use Service Bus for async, secure with Managed Identity + Key Vault, and instrument with Application Insights for end-to-end traces."*
